name: Contacts, read and write
plain: Reads the whole address book: names, numbers, emails, addresses.
meaning: Exposes the person's social graph and other people's private data. A shared favorite for growth teams and a historic abuse vector.

android.persistence: Until revoked; auto-reset after months unused (Android 11+)
android.store_policy: Play: contacts are sensitive data; Android 17 contacts write change for targets above 37
android.note: Android 17: CP2 limits account columns; WRITE_CONTACTS direct writes end for newer targets

ios.prompt_ui: Allow Full Access, Limit Access (iOS 18), Don't Allow
ios.store_policy: App Review 5.1.1(ii) and 5.1.2; no uploading contacts without consent
ios.note: iOS 13 hides the Notes field behind an entitlement

fields.name: contacts
fields.precision: all fields except notes on iOS

limits.headline: Can open your whole address book once you allow it, or only some on iPhone
limits.user_action: You tap Find friends or Import contacts
can: List names, numbers, emails and addresses
Add or change entries (Android with the extra permission)
Upload the list to match your friends
cannot: Open contacts before you tap Allow
Open the Notes field on iPhone without Apple's entitlement
Use a limited list on Android; it is all or one time pick
limits.differs: iPhone with iOS 18 and later offers Allow Full Access, Limit Access or Don't Allow; Android gives one choice for the whole contacts group.

story.what_it_is: Lets the app read and change your whole address book: names, numbers, emails and addresses.
story.for_you: You see a prompt to allow contacts. If you tap Allow, the app can see every person in your phone. Friends who never agreed to share are also shared.
story.for_makers: Contacts are the cheapest way to grow a social app. The app finds friends already in the network and sends invites. The data on other people is valuable, which is why platforms now steer apps to narrower options.

use_cases.example: A new social app matches your contacts to see who is already on it.
A chat app shows which friends are using it so you can start a chat.
A caller ID app names unknown callers from your contacts and a shared database.
A payment app finds friends to send money to.
A game finds friends so you can team up or send gifts.
A dating app hides your exes by matching contacts.
A contact manager cleans up duplicates and merges entries.

story.android_note: Android 17 limits account columns and ends direct write for newer target apps.
story.ios_note: iOS 13 hides the Notes field behind an entitlement, so passwords in notes are safer.

technical_bounds: Apps may not upload address book without consent
Android 17 limits account columns without READ_CONTACTS

abuse: Harvesting contacts to build shadow social graphs

linkedin.how: LinkedIn Android and iOS use contacts permission for address book sync and People You May Know

history.change: Contact Picker and tighter CP2 columns
